key_insight: In thin 316L foil laser welding, keyhole instability can trigger hole nucleation and rapid hole growth, with stability lost when the hole length approaches the sheet thickness.
engineering_relevance: The results define line-energy thresholds and a force-balance criterion that can help welders avoid perforation and cut-through in ultra-thin sheet lap joints.
method: High-speed imaging of laser keyhole welding on 100 μm 316L sheets (modeled with 200 μm foils)
Mapped the sequence from keyhole instability to hole nucleation and growth versus line energy
Used a Young-Laplace-based geometric stability balance to explain hole expansion
evidence_signal: The abstract reports continuous seams up to about 7 kJ/m, hole formation beyond that range, cutting above about 12 kJ/m, and hole growth at roughly 0.8–1.2 m/s over 1–3 ms.
watch_item: The stability criterion is derived from a specific thin-foil geometry and material system, so threshold values may shift for different thicknesses, alloys, or shielding/process conditions.
paper_title: Rupture and growth of holes in the melt pool during laser keyhole welding of thin sheets
